english.title: Adult employ a child for lottery / football pools - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) employed a child aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..) to provide facilities for gambling in connection with

(A)_[a lottery]_
(B)_[football pools]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 52 and 62(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
employed a child
to provide facilities for gambling in connection with
a lottery other than the National Lottery/football pools

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence does not apply to a lottery which forms part of the National Lottery.
(ii) This offence applies to adults, aged 18 or over, only; for young persons see the offence wording GA05100/H8279.
(iii) Section 45 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "child" means an individual who is less than 16 years old.
(iv) Section 63 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides the defence of reasonable belief about a person's age.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
